Exports from `@williamthorsen/toolbelt.statistics/candidate` the parameter, option, and result types of the normal-distribution functions, such as `ComputeCdfParams`, `IntervalProbabilities`, and `NormalDistributionFit`, together with `NormalDistributionParams`, which declares the optional `mean` and `standardDeviation` of a normal distribution. (#514)
Makes the `options` argument of `computeCdfInverse` optional, so that a call with a probability alone evaluates the standard normal distribution (mean 0, standard deviation 1). (#514)
Renames the `sdMin` and `sdMax` options of `findDistributionByIntervalProbability` to `minStandardDeviation` and `maxStandardDeviation`, matching the form of its `maxIterations` option. (#514)
items.migration: Rename `sdMin` to `minStandardDeviation` and `sdMax` to `maxStandardDeviation` in the options passed to `findDistributionByIntervalProbability`, and update any check on the text of its `RangeError` messages, which now name the new options; an untyped call that still passes the old names silently uses the default bounds of 0.01 and 20.

items.description: Changes three validation messages of `computeCdf`, `computeCdfInverse`, `computeNormalIntervalProbabilities`, and `findDistributionByIntervalProbability` to name the argument that they reject, such as `standardDeviation must be greater than 0.` in place of `Standard deviation must be greater than zero.`, which matches the package's other validation messages. (#520)
Fixes the issue that `computeCdf` returned `NaN` for a `NaN` mean, standard deviation, or value, and makes it throw a `TypeError` for a non-finite mean or standard deviation or a `NaN` value. (#511)

Fixes the issue that `computeCdfInverse` returned `NaN` for a `NaN` standard deviation and an infinite value for a probability outside [0, 1], and makes it throw a `TypeError` for a non-finite argument and a `RangeError` for such a probability. (#511)

Fixes the issue that `findDistributionByIntervalProbability` accepted a `tolerance` at or below 0, which the search can never meet, and returned `converged: false` after running every iteration, and makes it throw a `RangeError` for such a tolerance. (#511)

Fixes the issue that the bound checks of `@williamthorsen/toolbelt.statistics`, such as those rejecting a non-positive `standardDeviation` or `nIntervals`, threw a plain `Error` rather than a `RangeError`, and keeps each check's message. (#511)
Fixes the issue that `toCumulativeSumsFromAddends` returned the input array itself, rather than a new array, when the input was empty. (#513)
Fixes the issue that `toAddendsFromCumulativeSums` returned the input array itself for an empty input, so a caller that mutated the result also mutated the input. (#519)
Wraps the module-level helpers of `computeNormalIntervalProbabilities` and `findDistributionByIntervalProbability` in `region | Helpers` blocks. (#511)
Replaces the loop in `computeNormalIntervalProbabilities` that repeated `toAddendsFromCumulativeSums` with a call to that function. (#513)

Moves `evaluatePolynomial` and `evaluateRatio` from `computeErfc.ts` into `internal/polynomials.ts` and evaluates the Acklam coefficient tables of `computeCdfInverse`, now stored in ascending order, through them rather than through inline Horner expressions. (#521)

Tightens every tolerance in the `computeNormalIntervalProbabilities` tests to 9 decimal digits, which covers only the rounding of the listed expectations, and removes the references to a CDF approximation from the statistics test comments. (#512)

Changes the rejection tables in the tests of the four functions to check each error's class and a message fragment instead of the whole message, and adds rows for the `nIntervals` and `maxIterations` checks of `findDistributionByIntervalProbability`. (#520)

Fix computeCdf and computeCdfInverse accuracy in the normal tails (#326)
items.body:
- Fixes the lower-tail results of `computeCdf`, which had a relative error of 5e-5 at −3σ and 1.8e-2 at −8σ and were 0 below about −9σ, and makes them match reference values to a relative error of 1e-12 down to −30σ.
- Fixes `computeCdfInverse`, which was accurate only to about 1e-9, so that a round trip through `computeCdf` recovers the value within 1e-13 from −37σ to +3σ.

items.description: Remove the stale repo-local cliff.toml and normalize changelog titles (#327)
items.body:
- Stops `release-kit prepare` from printing a "skipped due to grouping error(s)" warning for each releasable workspace by letting it resolve the git-cliff template bundled with release-kit, previously overridden by the root `cliff.toml`.
- Excludes commits without a ticket prefix from future changelog entries.
- Renames the section titles in every `packages/*/.meta/changelog.json`, except `Dependency updates`, to the headings of release-kit's work-type taxonomy, such as "🎉 Features" and "🏗️ Internal features", and regenerates each `CHANGELOG.md` so that release-kit orders existing and new sections by the same rule.
- Causes the next `release-kit prepare` to plan patch releases of `dstructs`, `hof`, and `sets`, which had no other commits since their last release, because the changelog commit touches every workspace.

Fix unsound narrowing in `getAtIndexOrThrow` and rename it to `getItemAtIndexOrThrow` (#152)
items.body:
Fixes an issue where `getAtIndexOrThrow` could falsely treat an `undefined` return value as satisfying a return type that excluded `undefined`. The function now throws a `RangeError` if the array holds no item at the index and a `TypeError` if the index is not a safe integer. `undefined` is a valid return value if the input array's type allows `undefined` elements. The function is renamed `getItemAtIndexOrThrow`.

Separately, `findOrThrow` now decides a match by its predicate rather than by the value it found, so an element is not treated as not found merely because it is falsy. Its return type is now `T` rather than `NonNullable<T>`.

Migration: Consumers of `@williamthorsen/toolbelt.arrays/candidate` import `getItemAtIndexOrThrow` in place of `getAtIndexOrThrow`.

items.body: Adopts a pnpm catalog to avoid specifying the version of a common dependency in multiple places. Separately, fixes violations of newly activated `package-json` lint rules. Missing values have been added to `package.json` fields across the repo, and package descriptions are improved.

items.description: Rename get* functions by return kind and verb specificity (#119)
items.body: Renames thirteen functions across various packages to align with a consistent naming pattern.

items.description: Align stray modules with layout and TypeScript conventions (#118)
items.body: Aligns all packages with code-layout and annotation conventions, ending a handful of long-standing exceptions. Documentation has been updated to make the conventions clear.

items.description: Correct standard-deviation semantics in statistics normal-distribution functions (#93)
items.body:
The `standardDeviation` parameter now means the standard deviation throughout the package's normal-distribution functions, where it previously behaved as the variance. Callers who pass the default of 1 see unchanged output; any other value now yields different numbers. A standard deviation of 0 now places all mass at the mean, where it previously spread mass evenly across every interval; an even spread is now what a very large standard deviation approaches.

`getNormalIntervalProbabilities` accepts a new optional `halfWidth` that sizes the window it slices into intervals, defaulting to 3. `findDistributionByIntervalProbability` now takes its search controls as a second argument and reports whether the search converged, measures `tolerance` as a fraction of the target rather than as an absolute difference, and rejects an unreachable target with an error naming the bound it fell outside and the probability reachable there. Both functions now reject any numeric input that is not a finite number, instead of silently returning NaN results.

items.description: Fix slug punctuation and require safe integers (#86)
items.body:
- Fixes an issue where the use of certain letters as the slug separator in `slugify` would leave punctuation marks in the result.
- Time-unit conversions, scaling range bounds, normal-distribution interval counts, and array indices in object paths now reject values too large to represent exactly instead of silently losing precision.
- Seeded number generators now produce distinct sequences for seeds at or beyond 2^53, where adjacent seeds previously collapsed onto nearly identical output. A seed of that size saved before this release no longer reproduces the same output.

items.description: Fix deferred violations of unicorn lint rules (#88)
items.body: Fixes issues surfaced by `unicorn` lint rules that were temporarily downgraded to warnings and restores the rules to "error" severity. Separately, the `Queue` class in `dstructs` has been modified to hide its internal array.

items.description: Migrate Vitest configs to the nmr projects model (#73)
items.body: Packages no longer need to declare their own Vitest config. Test suites are now selected by a test file's name suffix rather than by choosing a config file: `*.app.test.ts` and `*.int.test.ts` route to the app and integration suites, and everything else runs as a unit test. Local development is now declared to require Node 24.16 or later.

items.description: Adopt the mechanical-syntax deferred unicorn rules (#82)
items.body: Promotes ten deferred lint rules from warnings to errors and fixes the issues surfaced by those rules. One published behavior changes as well: Converting a Map to a plain object no longer drops an entry keyed `__proto__`.

items.description: Use identical compiler settings for all packages (#105)
items.body: All packages now have identical compiler settings, using the settings from the `@williamthorsen/tsconfig` base config without modification.

items.description: Add dstructs and statistics packages (#58)
items.body: The toolbelt monorepo gains two more packages: `@williamthorsen/toolbelt.dstructs`, a first-in-first-out queue, and `@williamthorsen/toolbelt.statistics`, normal-distribution and cumulative-sum utilities with no third-party runtime dependency. Both reproduce the API from their earlier GitHub Packages releases and expose it at the candidate subpath (`@williamthorsen/toolbelt.{pkg}/candidate`).
